### Position read
The opponent opened Red from (0,3) to central (3,3). We answered Blue (4,7)->(4,4), occupying a second center square without standing directly between Red pieces. No losses or eliminations.

### Our plan
Deny center occupation first. Use Green to approach the center or build same-color flanks, while keeping Blue (4,4) supported tactically. Watch for Yellow entering (4,3) or (3,4). Seek sandwiches only with matching-color endpoints; never assume our two colors can pair.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent’s first move was an immediate central claim, suggesting a center-occupation strategy.

### Lessons
A piece on (3,4) would be vulnerable to Red landing at (3,5) with Red already at (3,3); (4,4) is the safer Blue center.

### Position read
Center is split: opponent pieces occupy (3,3) and (4,3), while we hold (4,4); (3,4) remains empty. Green moved (2,0)->(2,4), blocking the top-edge Red at (0,4) from moving straight into (3,4). No losses or eliminations.

### Our plan
Prioritize control of (3,4). Green at (2,4) can descend there if it remains open, giving us two central squares and preventing an opponent center win. If Red shifts its central piece from (3,3) to (3,4), look for a route into the vacated (3,3). Preserve Blue at (4,4) and check every move for same-color sandwich endpoints.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent has committed both early moves to adjacent central squares, strongly signaling a center strategy.

### Lessons
Blocking travel lanes can be as important as occupying the center. Teammate pieces do not complete sandwiches and can be friendly-fire casualties.

### Position read
The center is fully occupied but split: the opponent holds (3,3) and (4,3), while we hold (3,4) and (4,4), both with Blue. Green at (2,4) supports the central file. No losses or eliminations.

### Our plan
Preserve both Blue center pieces and seek a safe way to dislodge or capture one of the opponent’s left-center pieces. Green can reposition around the center, but avoid moves that create friendly-fire lines through Blue. Check whether Green can establish same-color endpoints around (3,3) or (4,3), and watch for opponent moves that vacate a center square.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent remains committed to central occupation and used Red’s latest move to clear its former top-edge route while retaining (3,3).

### Lessons
When the center is split two-and-two, maintaining both occupied squares denies immediate center victory. Always test central moves for sandwich captures in all four directions.

### Position read
We hold Blue at (3,4); the opponent holds Red at (3,3) and Yellow at (4,3), while (4,4) is empty. Blue has one loss. Yellow just captured our former Blue at (4,4). Green moved from (2,4) to (2,5).

### Our plan
The Green move blocks Red’s direct route from (0,5) to (3,5), which would sandwich and capture Blue at (3,4) against Red at (3,3). Preserve the remaining central Blue while developing same-color Green endpoints around the opponent’s center pieces. On Blue turns, check for ways to reinforce or retake (4,4) without exposing a sandwich.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent is actively attacking our center occupation and used Yellow at (4,5) to sandwich Blue at (4,4) against Yellow at (4,3). Red remains positioned as a potential sandwich endpoint at (3,3).

### Lessons
Same-team pieces do not form capture endpoints: Red could capture Blue at (3,4) using Red endpoints even though Yellow also occupies the center. Before every move, inspect open rook lanes that let an opponent land beside a central piece.

### Position read
We have Blue at (4,4), safely between opposing Yellow pieces at (4,3) and (4,5); moving into a sandwich does not trigger capture. The opponent holds Red at (3,3), Yellow at (4,3), and the other center square (3,4) is empty. Blue has one loss. Red’s move to (3,6) had threatened to land at (3,5) and sandwich our former Blue at (3,4) against Red at (3,3), so we withdrew it.

### Our plan
Preserve Blue at (4,4) and contest (3,4). Seek same-color endpoints to capture the central Red or Yellow pieces: with Blue fixed at (4,4), a future Blue landing at (4,2) could capture Yellow at (4,3). Develop another Blue toward column 2 while Green approaches useful central lanes without blocking Blue.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent is coordinating separate same-color endpoints around the center and proactively creating landing-square threats. Red rerouted from the top edge to (3,6) after its direct file was obstructed.

### Lessons
A piece may safely move into an already sandwiched square because only the mover can trigger capture. Recheck every new opponent rook lane for a landing square adjacent to our piece with a same-color far endpoint.

### Position read
We have Blue at (4,4); Yellow at (3,5) can later land at (4,5) to sandwich it against Yellow (4,3), so Blue must address that on its next turn. Green now occupies (2,5) and (5,5), with Yellow between them at (3,5) and (4,5) empty. The opponent holds center squares (3,3) and (4,3); we hold (4,4).

### Our plan
If Yellow stays at (3,5), play Green (5,5)->(4,5) to capture it against Green (2,5). On Blue’s next turn, either remove the central Yellow at (4,3) using a same-color pincer if available or withdraw (4,4) from the immediate Yellow sandwich. Continue contesting (3,4) while preserving our central foothold.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent coordinates same-color endpoints around the center and creates one-move sandwich threats. Yellow’s shift from (4,5) to (3,5) opened (4,5) as a capturing landing square against our Blue.

### Lessons
Moving into an existing sandwich is safe, but the resulting piece may be vulnerable to a later landing-square trigger. Before each move, inspect all empty squares adjacent to our pieces that complete an opponent same-color line.

### Position read
We moved Blue from (4,4) to center (3,4), escaping the threatened Yellow landing at (4,5). The opponent holds (3,3) with Red and (4,3) with Yellow. Green endpoints at (2,5) and (5,5) constrain Yellow (3,5).

### Our plan
On Green’s turn, capture on column 5 if available: if Yellow remains at (3,5) and (4,5) is empty, play (5,5)->(4,5); if Yellow moves from (3,5) to (4,5) and (3,5) is empty, play (2,5)->(3,5). If the opponent blocks both landing squares with pieces, preserve the net and strengthen the center. Blue should retain (3,4) if safe and look for a future Blue landing at (3,7) once the line to the Blue endpoint is continuous.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent coordinates same-color sandwich endpoints and may defend threatened pieces by filling capture landing squares with another piece.

### Lessons
Re-evaluate capture nets after every intervening opponent move: occupying the required landing square prevents the capture even when both same-color endpoints remain.

### Position read
Green moved (5,5)->(4,5), capturing Yellow at (3,5) against Green at (2,5). The center remains split: the opponent occupies (3,3), (4,3), and (4,4), while we occupy (3,4). Yellow now has 1 loss; our losses remain Blue 1, Green 0. Green at (4,5) directly borders the central Yellow at (4,4).

### Our plan
Preserve Blue at (3,4) and prevent the opponent from completing all four center squares. Seek same-color sandwich geometry against the central cluster, especially using Green (4,5) and existing Green anchors. On Blue turns, examine whether a safe move can capture along row 3 or reinforce a center square without exposing immediate occupation. Track any attack on Blue (3,4), since vacating it could enable center victory.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent prioritizes central occupation and used Yellow (7,4)->(4,4) despite leaving another Yellow in a prepared Green sandwich.

### Lessons
Execute a prepared capture when the landing square and endpoint remain available, but immediately reassess whether the resulting piece can be counter-sandwiched or whether center occupation creates an instant threat.

### Position read
The opponent controls three center squares: Red (3,3), Yellow (4,3), and Yellow (4,4); (3,4) is empty. Yellow can win immediately next turn by moving (4,4)->(3,4). Blue has 2 losses and only four pieces remaining. No legal Blue move this turn can occupy (3,4), capture a central piece, or obstruct that winning move.

### Our plan
Blue moved (5,7)->(5,4), placing pressure beneath the central Yellow cluster if play continues. If the opponent misses center victory, prioritize disrupting or occupying a center square immediately. Avoid any Blue capture loss because one more eliminates Blue.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent strongly prioritizes central occupation and has now converted a Red sandwich capture into a direct one-move center win.

### Lessons
After losing the center defender, check every opposing color’s immediate rook access to the vacated central square. Team-mixed center occupation wins even though same-color pairing is required for sandwiches.

### Position read
The opponent occupies (3,3), (4,3), and (4,4), with (3,4) empty. Green cannot legally occupy (3,4), capture a central piece, or otherwise prevent center completion. Red at (2,4) can move directly to (3,4) next turn for an immediate win; Yellow at (4,4) can also reach it later.

### Our plan
Green moved (3,0)->(3,2), advancing beside the central Red piece in the best available continuation. If the immediate win is missed, use Blue or Green’s next opportunity to remove or occupy a center square.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent prioritizes the center but previously chose a Green capture instead of taking the available center win.

### Lessons
Before each move, test every opponent piece sharing a row or column with the last empty center square. A mixed-color team completes center occupation instantly.
